title: How to kill the Wall obstruction when upgrading an FH(ℚ) complex?
question:
Let X be a finite CW complex whose rational homology agrees with that of a closed n-manifold (an FH(\mathbb Q) complex in our notation), and assume \pi_1(X)=\Gamma carries the 2-torsion lattice used in the proof. Suppose a degree-one normal map f:M^n	o X with stable normal bundle classified by 
u has already been built. Wall's surgery exact sequence says that the obstruction to replacing X by a closed manifold M' homotopy equivalent to X is the element

	heta(\eta(f)) \in L_n^{\langle1angle}(\mathbb Z[\Gamma]),

where \eta(f)\in[X,G/TOP] is the normal invariant of f. Which conditions on \eta(f) and on the L-group ensure this obstruction vanishes, and how does one see that the torsion in \Gamma does not reintroduce an obstruction while keeping \pi_1(M')\cong\Gamma?
answer:
Because X is a rational Poincar'e complex, the usual Postnikov tower plus Sullivan's rational surgery produces a degree-one normal map f whose normal invariant lives in [X,G/TOP]\cong H^0(X;\mathbb Z/2)\oplus H^2(X;\mathbb Z/2)\oplus H^4(X;\mathbb Z)\oplus\cdots. Changing f within its bordism class changes \eta(f) by an arbitrary element of this cohomology group, so we may hunt for \eta with trivial Wall obstruction. The relevant part of the exact sequence

0	o S^{TOP}(X)	o[X,G/TOP]\xrightarrow{	heta} L_n^{\langle1angle}(\mathbb Z[\Gamma])	o0

pairs each normal invariant with its surgery obstruction. For the chosen 2-torsion lattice, the assembly map identifies L_n^{\langle1angle}(\mathbb Z[\Gamma])\otimes\mathbb Q with H_n(B\Gamma;\mathbb Q)\oplus H_{n-4}(B\Gamma;\mathbb Q)\oplus\cdots, but B\Gamma=B K has only even-dimensional rational homology inherited from the FH(\mathbb Q) model. The summands in degree n, n-4, ... all vanish because torsion in \Gamma forces these groups to be finite, hence zero after tensoring with \mathbb Q. Thus L_n^{\langle1angle}(\mathbb Z[\Gamma]) is torsion, generated by 2-primary classes detected by the reduced w_2 and w_4 of the normal invariant. By choosing \eta(f) so that these characteristic classes match those of the FH(\mathbb Q) tangent microbundle, we force 	heta(\eta(f))=0.

With the obstruction gone, the exact sequence shows that \eta(f) lifts to an element of the structure set S^{TOP}(X), i.e. to a closed manifold M' together with a simple homotopy equivalence M'	o X inducing an isomorphism on \pi_1. Normal invariants that differ by elements of [X,G/TOP] correspond to performing tangential surgeries on embedded spheres; these do not change \pi_1 because all handles of index 1 and n-1 are attached along null-homotopic loops (the attaching spheres represent zero in H_1 thanks to FH(\mathbb Q)). Consequently M' is a closed manifold, shares \pi_1 with X, and realizes the FH(\mathbb Q) data once the L-group obstruction is neutralized.
